title: Shape the home page: a blog that is visibly yours
question: Three ways to put you, visibly, at the centre of the home page. Your photo, your name and your notes are present in each; the chronological feed stays; 'new here?' is a small aside. Lock one, steer it, or re-roll.

options.label: Letterhead
options.lineage: a personal letterhead and a letter
options.thesis: Your signature is the wordmark and the home page reads as a letter from you: greeting, your writing, then a P.S.
materials: your photo in a chalk frame
options.viewport: Signature 'Ish' as the masthead over a ruled letterhead line, your photo and a two-line greeting, the dated feed, and a P.S. pointing new QA leads to two posts.
options.risk: Wants your real signature scanned in; the greeting is draft copy you would rewrite.

options.label: Margin notes from Ish
options.lineage: an author annotating their own notebook
options.thesis: Every post in the feed carries your own handwritten margin note on why you wrote it.
options.viewport: Your photo, name and roles across the top with a small 'new here?' aside; each feed entry pairs the post with a one-line note in your hand.
options.risk: Only feels personal if you write the notes; posts without one fall back to plain entries.

options.label: Author column
options.lineage: the classic personal blog, author always in view
options.thesis: The writing leads in the main column while you stay present in a column beside it on every page.
options.viewport: Main column opens with your newest post large (title + first lines), then older posts; the side column holds your photo, signature, roles, a 'Now' note, links and 'new here?'.
options.risk: The 'Now' note goes stale unless you update it; the column moves below the feed on phones.
